pois.name: Église Saint-Sulpice
pois.description: Paris's second-largest church (73m twin towers), with Delacroix murals and a gnomon meridian line immortalised in The Da Vinci Code.

pois.name: Palais du Luxembourg
pois.description: Marie de Médici's 1625 palace, now the French Senate. Its garden — 23 hectares — is Paris's favourite green lung, with the famous Medici Fountain.

pois.name: Musée d'Orsay
pois.description: The world's largest Impressionist collection inside a converted 1900 Beaux-Arts railway station. Monet, Renoir, Van Gogh, Cézanne.

pois.name: Café de Flore
pois.description: Founded 1887. Sartre and de Beauvoir wrote here every morning for a decade. Still serves the best hot chocolate in Paris on the terrace.

pois.name: Musée Delacroix
pois.description: Eugène Delacroix's last atelier in a small garden off the Place Furstenberg — the most intimate museum in Paris.
